meta.scene_summary: We're busy building the future of AI while the present infrastructure is busy forgetting how to do its basic job.

cooking.headline: Nvidia is making so much money that the sales reports have gone into witness protection.
cooking.summary: When you hit $104 billion in revenue, you stop itemizing the receipt and just start buying the store. It turns out that when you become the global dealer for AI chips, you don't really have to explain your sales strategy to anyone anymore.
cooking.plain_english: Nvidia has stopped publicly disclosing specific sales data for Singapore following a period of massive revenue growth.

cooking.headline: Jensen Huang is pulling a classic 'I might come back' move
cooking.summary: Jensen Huang resigned and immediately realized that watching the company from the sidelines is significantly less fun than running the show. It's the corporate equivalent of leaving a party only to realize you left your phone inside.
cooking.plain_english: Jensen Huang has indicated he is willing to return to his former role at Nvidia shortly after announcing his resignation.

cooking.headline: Windows 11 is now acting like the group project partner who watches you work.
cooking.summary: Microsoft is tracking exactly which coding tools you use, because apparently, they need to know which IDE is helping you write the bugs they'll eventually patch. It's like having a manager hover over your shoulder, but with more telemetry and less helpful advice.
cooking.plain_english: Windows 11 collects and stores information regarding the specific software and coding tools developers use on their systems.

cooked.headline: The US national security network just hit a 404, proving even the Pentagon has bad days
cooked.summary: The highly classified network meant to handle the nation's biggest secrets apparently went down for an unplanned maintenance break. It turns out that even the most secure infrastructure in the world is still just a collection of servers that can be brought down by a bad update or a loose cable.
cooked.plain_english: A secure communication system used by the United States government for classified information experienced a service outage.

cooked.headline: Optimizely turned every major news site into a malware delivery service
cooked.summary: Optimizely had their supply chain compromised, effectively turning the world's most trusted news outlets into unsuspecting malware distributors. It's the digital equivalent of trusting your friend to hold your bag and realizing they've been using it to smuggle contraband the whole time.
cooked.plain_english: Hackers compromised Optimizely's software, allowing them to place malicious code on the websites of several major media organizations and companies.

cooked.headline: Java 17 just dropped a pre-auth RCE, because security is just a suggestion now.
cooked.summary: We really thought we were past the era of 'oops, remote code execution,' but Java 17 decided to bring that vintage energy back. It's the digital equivalent of finding out your front door lock was actually just a sticker of a lock.
cooked.plain_english: A critical security vulnerability has been discovered in Java 17 that allows unauthorized attackers to remotely execute code on affected servers.

cooked.headline: The AI gold rush is hitting the 'where is the money' phase
cooked.summary: Baidu and Xiaomi CEOs are finally noticing that burning billions on GPU clusters isn't quite paying the rent yet. It turns out that 'AI-powered' isn't a substitute for a business model that actually generates profit.
cooked.plain_english: The leaders of Baidu and Xiaomi are concerned that the massive financial investment in artificial intelligence is not resulting in sufficient revenue.

cooked.headline: Apple services are down, reminding us that the cloud is just someone else's computer on vacation.
cooked.summary: Apple's ecosystem hit a wall today, proving that even a trillion-dollar company can't escape the 'it works on my machine' paradox. It turns out that when the mothership goes offline, your expensive hardware becomes a very sleek, very minimalist paperweight.
cooked.plain_english: Apple is experiencing technical problems that have made several of their online services unavailable to users.

cooked.headline: United Airlines is having a system outage, effectively turning the airport into a very expensive waiting room.
cooked.summary: United is dealing with a major system failure, which is the aviation equivalent of a production deployment gone horribly wrong on a Friday afternoon. At least when your code breaks, you don't have to explain to a hundred people why they're stuck in a terminal for six hours.
cooked.plain_english: United Airlines is suffering from a widespread computer system failure that has caused significant disruptions to their flight operations.

cooked.headline: The 'note-taking app that thinks for you' has decided to stop thinking entirely.
cooked.summary: Mem promised to build a second brain for your notes, but apparently, even the smartest AI can't manage its own business model. It turns out that offloading your memory to a startup is only a good idea if the startup lasts longer than your actual brain cells.
cooked.plain_english: The note-taking application Mem is shutting down and users must export their data before the service closes.
